chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
Entering the Ka'bah is an entry into the mercy of Allah, and exiting it is an exit from sins, protected in what remains of his life, and forgiven for what has passed of his sins.

key_terms.الذُّنُوبِ: sins; acts of disobedience for which one bears moral burden
key_terms.الْخُرُوجُ: exiting; departing from the sacred place
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Ka'bah, the Sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.دُخُولُ: entering; the act of going into the sacred space
key_terms.عُمُرِهِ: his life; the remainder of a person's lifespan
key_terms.مَعْصُومٌ: protected; preserved from falling into sin
key_terms.مَغْفُورٌ: forgiven; having one's past sins pardoned

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of entering the Ka'bah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes entering the Ka'bah as entering into the mercy of Allah and leaving it as leaving behind sins. It conveys the spiritual purification, protection, and forgiveness associated with this sacred act during hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Entering the Kaaba is an entry into the mercy of Allah (swt), and exiting it is an exit from sins, making one protected for the remainder of their life, with forgiveness granted for all past sins."
